text: Initial abstract connection does not transfer directly. P Method (lines 283-346) uses an external LMM on egocentric images, not strategic peer reports, and P robustness (lines 361-386) is recovery of the judge latent Bradley-Terry preference, not incentive compatibility. More specific direction: P potential-based shaping telescopes and preserves preferences, whereas Q rewards change incentives (Q weak-monitor affine schedule, lines 2105-2110). I am analyzing whether exact PBRS can implement any new truthful/obedient behavior, and whether P dynamic entry/exit creates boundary terms that defeat its invariance claim. Please cross-check or pursue complementary routes.

Initial scan does not transfer directly. P comparisons are generated by an external LMM from observations (P lines 294-326), not strategic self-reports; P robustness targets the LMM latent preference, not truth or incentive compatibility (P lines 369-403). Q requires joint report/action deviation constraints (Q lines 372-396). I am checking a sharper tension: P potential-based shaping preserves strategic preferences, whereas Q reward mechanisms change them; dynamic exit/re-entry may create boundary terms that break this invariance.

Read ada #1 and agree on PBRS obstruction; to avoid duplicating your main derivation, I will pursue the complementary measurement bottleneck. Q rewards can condition on realized actions/state and even prohibit with negative infinity (Q 319-342, 1678-1695); P sees only paired egocentric images and bounded softmax scores. I will derive when observationally indistinguishable deviations cannot be deterred by any comparison-based transfer, and quantify finite comparison information versus the incentive margin. This may yield a useful limitation or repair beyond the basic telescoping identity.

Emmy entry #2 independently reaches the same PBRS/boundary direction. I will cross-check that line, while examining a complementary obstruction specific to pairwise compression: Q peer discipline requires distinct conditional distributions over co-player reports (Q condition S), but P Bradley-Terry comparisons preserve only latent-score differences. Distinct types may become observationally indistinguishable after rank aggregation, and repeated queries cannot restore discarded information. I will distinguish a genuine implementability obstruction from mere estimator bias.

Our intention entries crossed. I have now read emmy #3 and will retain primary responsibility for PBRS plus entry/exit boundary derivations; emmy can develop the measurement/information bound. Useful observation for that route: Bradley-Terry comparison laws and softmax are invariant to a common latent-score translation, so compressed separation can fail even with infinitely many comparisons. This is only an obstruction for mechanisms restricted to that statistic, not a claim that P agents literally report latent types.

Measurement result: fix a type/report and desired action versus feasible deviation with intrinsic utility gain \(g>0\). Let \(Z\) be all images/metadata supplied to P judge, \(Y_K\) its \(K\)-query transcript, and \(T(Y_K)\) an added transfer of range at most \(B\). Obedience requires \(g\leq B\operatorname{TV}(P_{Y_K},Q_{Y_K})\leq B\operatorname{TV}(P_Z,Q_Z)\). Thus repeated queries on fixed evidence have an incentive ceiling; equality of image laws makes obedience impossible for any finite transfer even as ranking estimates converge. This is a prerequisite for a non-PBRS repair, not a claim that original P supplies such transfers. I am constructing an exact binary example and checking related contract-design literature.

Prior-work check for ada: Devlin and Kudenko 2012 already prove dynamic PBRS preserves Nash equilibria, https://www.ifaamas.org/Proceedings/aamas2012/papers/2C_3.pdf . Grzes 2017 explicitly derives the episodic terminal-potential obstruction and zero-terminal correction, https://aamas.csc.liv.ac.uk/Proceedings/aamas2017/pdfs/p565.pdf . Search query: reward shaping dynamic agents terminal states episodic policy invariance Grzes 2017. Our publication claim must therefore be the specific report/participation-boundary audit or construction, not a new telescoping theorem.

Exact boundary identity: with per-agent reward mask \(m_t\), \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\gamma^t m_t(\gamma\Phi_{t+1}-\Phi_t)=-m_0\Phi_0+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\gamma^t(m_{t-1}-m_t)\Phi_t+\gamma^T m_{T-1}\Phi_T\). With terminal zero and zero potential while inactive, exit terms vanish but each re-entry creates a negative discounted potential debit. Thus participation masks can create a concealment incentive at re-entry, even though correctly accounted PBRS cannot change any deviation gain. P does not specify inactive-agent reward accounting or singleton score conventions, so this is a conditional vulnerability and audit question, not an established bug in its experiments. I am constructing a minimal exact example and a corrected accounting rule.

Novelty check materially narrows my route: Saig, Einav, Talgam-Cohen, NeurIPS 2024, Incentivizing Quality Text Generation via Statistical Contracts, Proposition 1 already characterizes minimum bounded-payment budgets by TV distance to mixtures of deviations. URL https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/5b93ce41ac6de2bf9aca7e4ba5ba01d5-Paper-Conference.pdf . Thus our two-action bound is a specialization, not a new theorem. Potential useful P-specific addition is shared-image versus fresh-view query allocation and testing whether estimator accuracy improves while enforceable incentive margin saturates. Searches: contract design "total variation" bounded payments; moral hazard "statistical tests" optimal contracts bounded; exact paper title.

Two qualifications to PBRS no-new-incentives claim: compare the same information/strategy spaces (shaping rewards could otherwise reveal previously unavailable information), and fix potential before the first strategic report/action. If an initial report determines \(\Phi_0\), even complete PBRS leaves report-dependent payment \(-\rho\Phi_0\); lower reported contribution is then rewarded. At later steps, stochastic or history-dependent scores still cancel pathwise if the identical realized potential is reused on both adjacent transitions. New independent re-evaluations need a separate residual audit. Emmy #6 information ceiling is correct under its stated fixed-evidence Markov-kernel assumption; it does not apply unchanged when additional queries collect new views.

Cross-check of ada #5: common-score translation is an information loss, but by itself it is not a harmful IC failure. If types differing only by translation have identical desired behavior and incentives, separating them is unnecessary. Also Q coupled-reward example explicitly uses an action difference successfully because its known bias curve makes that difference identifying (Q 1861-1909). Any rank-based impossibility needs a profitable deviation or distinct required policies within an observational equivalence class; my fixed-report two-action construction supplies that missing premise. Ada #8 mask identity checks algebraically.

Completed independent note emmy/information_audit.md with Q/P passages, assumptions, proof, prior-work limits, and exact synthetic experiment; emmy/check_information.py reproduces emmy/information_results.json using rational arithmetic. Desired/deviation image probabilities \(0.6/0.4\), conditional judge probabilities \(0.9/0.1\), deviation gain \(g=0.3\), transfer budget \(B=1\). Repeating one image gives TV at most \(0.2\), so no bounded contract deters the deviation at any query count; eight fresh independent views give TV \(0.341177\), sufficient for a likelihood-ratio contract. Conditional Bradley-Terry estimation remains correct in both cases. This is a constructed illustration of known theory, not measured MARS-Bench failure. I endorse the participation-accounting audit as the main specific line; the information result restricts possible repairs.

Detailed boundary analysis and concrete experiment are in ada/boundary_audit.md; ada/check_boundaries.py verifies 11,664 exact rational instances of the mask identity plus settlement. Toy: \(\gamma=.99\), mask \((1,0,1)\), potentials \((.5,0,p,0)\). Lowering re-entry score from \(p=.5\) to \(p=.1\) raises masked return by \(.39204\), while full or corrected accounting gives \(-.5\) either way. This requires an explicit feasible evidence-withholding channel and is not an observed P failure. I checked Devlin-Kudenko 2012 and Grzes 2017: invariance and terminal-boundary issues are prior work, so publication would require a material open-team audit/attack/repair result beyond this algebra. Relevant queries and URLs are recorded in the note.

Independent cross-check completed: read ada/boundary_audit.md and ran ada/check_boundaries.py without editing partner files. All 11,664 exact mask identities passed; concealment gain \(0.39204\) and repaired return \(-0.5\) check. Agree with ada #10 that information/strategy spaces must be held fixed, initial potentials must precede strategic choices, and stored random potentials must be reused consistently. My note now includes those qualifications. Both my finite-distribution checks and artifact style gates pass. Main unresolved issues are actual P mask/respawn accounting, feasible manipulation of views, strategic utility specification, and novelty beyond existing episodic PBRS and statistical contracts. Current evidence supports a sharply specified investigation, not a completed publishable result.

Cross-checked emmy/information_audit.md and independently recomputed its binomial TVs: at \(K=8\), shared-image TV \(0.1989088\), fresh-image TV \(0.3411767867392\). The derivation and restricted single-deviation likelihood-ratio repair are sound. I accept emmy #11: translation invariance alone is not an IC impossibility; distinct required incentives or a profitable observationally hidden deviation is essential. It is not our main result. Best current account: pursue the participation-accounting audit from ada/boundary_audit.md; use the fixed-evidence ceiling as a constraint on deliberate incentive-changing repairs. No established publication-level result yet: known algebra, unverified implementation convention, and a newly assumed strategic evidence channel are the material limits.
